prayers.title: The Universal Prayer
prayers.note: Attributed to Pope Clement XI (died 1721). The translation is from General Catholic Devotions (New York, 1909), less one line of its intercessions whose names for other Christians and for unbelievers the Church no longer uses.
en: O my God, I believe in thee; do thou strengthen my faith.
All my hopes are in thee; do thou secure them.
I love thee with my whole heart; teach me to love thee more and more.
I am sorry that I have offended thee; do thou increase my sorrow.
I adore thee as my first beginning;
I aspire after thee as my last end.
I give thee thanks as my constant benefactor;
I call upon thee as my sovereign protector.
Vouchsafe, O my God, to conduct me by thy wisdom,
to restrain me by thy justice,
to comfort me by thy mercy,
to defend me by thy power.
To thee I desire to consecrate all my thoughts, my actions, and my sufferings,
that I henceforward may think only of thee, speak only of thee,
and ever refer all my actions to thy greater glory,
and suffer willingly whatever thou shalt appoint.
O Lord, I desire that in all things thy will be done,
because it is thy will,
and in the manner that thou willest.
I beg of thee to enlighten my understanding,
to inflame my will,
to purify my body,
and to sanctify my soul.
Give me strength, O my God, to expiate my offences,
to overcome my temptations,
to subdue my passions,
to acquire the virtues proper for my state.
Fill my heart with tender affection for thy goodness,
a hatred of my faults,
a love for my neighbour,
and a contempt for the world.
Let me always be submissive to my superiors,
condescending to my inferiors,
faithful to my friends,
and charitable to my enemies.
Assist me to overcome sensuality by mortification,
avarice by almsdeeds,
anger by meekness,
and tepidity by zeal.
O my God, make me prudent in my undertakings,
courageous in dangers,
patient in affliction,
and humble in prosperity.
Grant that I may be ever attentive at my prayers,
temperate at my meals,
diligent in my employments,
and constant in my resolutions.
Let my conscience be ever upright and pure,
my exterior modest,
my conversation edifying,
my comportment regular.
Assist me, that I may continually labour to overcome nature,
correspond with thy grace,
keep thy commandments,
and work out my salvation.
Discover to me, O my God, the nothingness of this world,
the greatness of heaven,
the shortness of time,
the length of eternity.
Grant that I may be prepared for death,
fear thy judgments,
escape hell,
and, in the end, obtain heaven.
All that I have asked for myself I confidently ask for others;
for my family, my relations, my benefactors, my friends,
and also for my enemies.
I ask it for the whole Church, for all the orders of which it is composed;
more especially for our Holy Father, the Pope;
for our bishop, for our pastors, and for all who are in authority;
also for all those for whom thou desirest that I should pray.
Give them, O Lord, all that thou knowest
to be conducive to thy glory and necessary for their salvation.
Strengthen the just in virtue, convert sinners,
console the afflicted,
give to the faithful departed rest and eternal life;
that together we may praise, love, and bless thee for all eternity. Amen.

prayers.title: Before Any Work
prayers.note: A collect of the Roman Missal, also said at the end of the Litany of the Saints.
en: Direct, we beseech thee, O Lord,
our actions by thy holy inspirations,
and carry them on by thy gracious assistance;
that every prayer and work of ours
may always begin from thee,
and by thee be happily ended.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: ut cuncta nostra oratio et operatio

prayers.title: Omnipotence of the Father
prayers.note: A short prayer to the Holy Trinity for the work of the day. From the Raccolta (1910).
en: Omnipotence of the Father, help my frailty,
and rescue me from the depths of misery.
Wisdom of the Son, direct all my thoughts, words, and actions.
Love of the Holy Spirit, be the source of all the operations of my soul,
so that they may be entirely conformed to the divine will.
la: et e profundo miseriae eripe me.
Sapientia Filii, dirige cogitationes, verba et actiones meas omnes.
Amor Spiritus Sancti, esto cunctarum animae meae operationum principium,
quo iugiter sint divino beneplacito conformes.

prayers.title: May the Will of God Be Done
prayers.note: A short act of resignation to the will of God. From the Raccolta, in the English of The New Raccolta (1903).
en: May the most just, most high, and most amiable will of God
be done in all things,
be praised and magnified forever.
la: Fiat, laudetur, atque in aeternum superexaltetur
iustissima, altissima et amabilissima voluntas Dei

prayers.title: In Time of Trial
prayers.note: For faithfulness when evil seems to have the upper hand. From The New Raccolta (1903).
en: Omnipotent Lord! who dost permit evil that good may spring from it,
listen to the humble prayers,
by which we ask of thee the grace of remaining faithful to thee, even unto death.
Grant us also, through the intercession of Mary ever blessed,
that we may always conform ourselves to thy most holy will.

prayers.title: For Mercy and Pardon
prayers.note: One of the prayers that close the Litany of the Saints.
en: O God, whose property it is always to have mercy and to spare,
receive our petitions,
that we, and all thy servants who are bound by the chain of sin,
may, in the compassion of thy goodness, mercifully be absolved.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Deus, cui proprium est misereri semper et parcere,
ut nos, et omnes famulos tuos, quos delictorum catena constringit,

prayers.title: For Purity of Heart
prayers.note: One of the prayers that close the Litany of the Saints. The reins are the inmost desires.
en: Inflame, O Lord, our reins and hearts
with the fire of the Holy Spirit;
to the end that we may serve thee with a chaste body,
and please thee with a clean heart.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: renes nostros et cor nostrum, Domine:

prayers.title: For Our Home and Our Kindred
prayers.note: From the Raccolta (1910).
en: Loosen, O Lord, we pray thee, in thy pity, the bonds of our sins,
and by the intercession of the blessed Mary ever Virgin, Mother of God,
Saint Joseph, the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and all saints,
keep us thy servants and our abodes in all holiness;
cleanse us, our relations, kinsfolk, and acquaintances from all vices;
adorn us with all virtues;
grant us peace and health;
repel our enemies visible and invisible;
curb our carnal desires;
give us healthful seasons;
bestow thy charity upon our friends and our enemies;
guard thy holy City;
preserve our Sovereign Pontiff N.;
defend all prelates, princes, and Christian people from all adversity.
Let thy blessing be ever upon us,
and grant to all the faithful departed eternal rest.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

prayers.title: Three Offerings for a Good Death
prayers.note: From the Raccolta (1910). Each offering is followed by an Our Father, a Hail Mary and a Glory Be.
en: We offer to the Most Holy Trinity the merits of Jesus Christ,
in thanksgiving for the Most Precious Blood which he shed in the garden for us;
and through those merits we beseech his Divine Majesty for pardon of our sins.
> our-father
> hail-mary
> glory-be
We offer to the Most Holy Trinity the merits of Jesus Christ,
in thanksgiving for his most precious death endured on the Cross for us;
and through those merits we beseech his Divine Majesty
for the remission of the pains due to our sins.
> our-father
> hail-mary
> glory-be
We offer to the Most Holy Trinity the merits of Jesus Christ,
in thanksgiving for his unspeakable charity,
in descending from heaven to earth to take human flesh,
and to suffer and die for us upon the Cross;
and by those merits we beseech his Divine Majesty
to bring our souls to the glory of heaven after our death.
> our-father
> hail-mary
> glory-be

prayers.title: For the Faithful Departed
prayers.note: The collect of the Mass of All Souls, also said at the end of the Litany of the Saints.
en: O God, the Creator and Redeemer of all the faithful,
grant to the souls of thy servants departed
the remission of all their sins,
that through pious supplications
they may obtain that pardon which they have always desired;
who livest and reignest with God the Father
in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God,
world without end. Amen.
la: Fidelium, Deus, omnium Conditor et Redemptor,
Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre,

prayers.title: For the Living and the Dead
prayers.note: The last of the prayers that close the Litany of the Saints.
en: Almighty and eternal God,
who hast dominion over the living and the dead,
and art merciful to all whom thou foreknowest shall be thine by faith and good works;
we humbly beseech thee that they for whom we have purposed to offer our prayers,
whether this present world still detains them in the flesh,
or the next world has already received them divested of their bodies,
may, by the clemency of thine own goodness and the intercession of thy saints,
obtain pardon and full remission of all their sins.
Through our Lord Jesus Christ,
who liveth and reigneth with thee in the unity of the Holy Spirit,
world without end. Amen.
la: qui vivorum dominaris simul et mortuorum,
omniumque misereris quos tuos fide et opere futuros esse praenoscis:
te supplices exoramus; ut, pro quibus effundere preces decrevimus,
quosque vel praesens saeculum adhuc in carne retinet,
vel futurum iam exutos corpore suscepit,
intercedentibus omnibus Sanctis tuis, pietatis tuae clementia,
Per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, Filium tuum,
qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate Spiritus Sancti, Deus,

prayers.title: For Peace
prayers.note: The antiphon and collect for peace of the Roman Breviary, as given in the Raccolta (1910).
en: Give peace, O Lord, in our days;
for there is none other that fighteth for us,
but only thou, our God.
V. Let there be peace in thy strength, O Lord.
R. And plenty in thy strong places.
! Let us pray.
O God, from whom proceed all holy desires,
all right counsels and just works;
grant unto us thy servants
that peace which the world cannot give,
that our hearts may be devoted to thy service,
and that, being delivered from the fear of our enemies,
we may pass our time in peace under thy protection.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Da pacem, Domine, in diebus nostris:
quia non est alius qui pugnet pro nobis,
V. Fiat pax in virtute tua.
R. Et abundantia in turribus tuis.
recta consilia, et iusta sunt opera:
quam mundus dare non potest, pacem:
ut et corda nostra mandatis tuis dedita,

prayers.title: For Peace and Order in the World
prayers.note: From the Raccolta (1910), where it is dated 1889, under Pope Leo XIII.
en: Thou seest, O Lord, how on all sides the winds are let loose upon us,
and the sea is growing rough with the violent commotion of the waves.
Do thou, we beseech thee, who alone art able,
command the winds and the waves.
Restore to mankind that true peace which the world cannot give,
the peace which comes of good order.
Let men impelled by thy grace
return to a right and orderly course of life,
practising again, as they ought, love towards God,
justice and charity in dealing with their neighbour,
temperance and self-control in their own lives.
May thy kingdom come,
and may those who now vainly and laboriously seek for truth and salvation,
far removed from thee,
understand that they must live as thy servants in subjection to thee.
Thy laws show forth thy justice and paternal gentleness,
and to enable us to keep them,
thou dost freely supply by thy grace the ready means.
The life of man on earth is a warfare,
but “thou dost thyself behold the strife,
thou dost help man to conquer,
raise him when he falls,
and crown him when he is victorious.”

prayers.title: For the Conversion of Sinners
prayers.note: An offering for the Church, the holy souls and sinners. From The New Raccolta (1903).
en: Eternal Father, we offer thee the blood, the passion, and the death of Jesus Christ,
the sorrows of Mary most holy, and of Saint Joseph,
in satisfaction for our sins,
in aid of the holy souls in purgatory,
for the needs of holy Mother Church,
and for the conversion of sinners.

prayers.title: Prayer of Saint Alphonsus to Our Lady
prayers.note: Saint Alphonsus Liguori. From General Catholic Devotions (1909).
en: Most holy and immaculate virgin, O my Mother,
thou who art the Mother of my Lord, the queen of the world,
the advocate, hope, and refuge of sinners!
I, the most wretched among them, come now to thee.
I venerate thee, great queen,
and give thee thanks for the many favors thou hast bestowed on me in the past.
Most of all do I thank thee for having saved me from hell, which I so often deserved.
I love thee, Lady most worthy of love,
and by the love which I bear thee I promise ever in the future to serve thee,
and to do what in me lies to win others to thy love.
In thee I put all my trust, all my hope of salvation.
Receive me as thy servant,
and cover me with the mantle of thy protection,
thou who art the Mother of mercy!
And since thou hast so much power with God,
deliver me from all temptations,
or at least obtain for me the grace ever to overcome them.
From thee I ask a true love of Jesus Christ, and the grace of a happy death.
O my Mother, by thy love for God I beseech thee to be at all times my helper,
but above all at the last moment of my life.
Leave me not until thou seest me safely in heaven,
there for endless ages to bless thee and sing thy praises. Amen.

prayers.title: On Waking
prayers.note: From General Catholic Devotions (New York, 1909), to be said with the sign of the cross on rising.
en: I rise in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ,
who redeemed me by his precious blood.
Bless, guide, and protect me from all evil, O Lord!
Strengthen me to all good and lead me to eternal life. Amen.

prayers.title: Before Sleep
prayers.note: A prayer of Saint Alphonsus Liguori (died 1787), in the English of General Catholic Devotions (New York, 1909).
en: My Lord and God Jesus Christ!
I adore thee and give thee thanks for all the graces
which thou hast granted me to-day.
I offer up to thee my rest and every moment of this night,
and implore thee to preserve me from all sin.
Therefore I place myself into the wound of thy sacred side,
and beneath the protecting mantle of my Mother Mary.
May thy holy angels assist me and watch over my peace,
and may thy holy blessing remain with me.

prayers.title: Before Confession
prayers.note: From General Catholic Devotions (New York, 1909).
en: Merciful God! I give infinite thanks to thee
for the many and great graces thou hast bestowed upon me during my whole life.
Would that I had never been ungrateful to thee,
that I never had offended thee.
But I have sinned exceedingly and often,
and have done so again since my last confession.
Therefore I come to thee, imploring thee in profoundest humility
to give me thy light and thy grace,
that I may know and acknowledge all my sins, faults, and transgressions,
be truly sorry for them, sincerely confess them,
do penance, and amend my life;
for thy greater glory and for the salvation of my soul.
! Examine your conscience.
# Before going in
The Lord be in my heart and on my lips
that I may worthily and competently confess my sins.

prayers.title: After Confession
prayers.note: From General Catholic Devotions (New York, 1909). The Holy Helpers are the fourteen saints long invoked together in need.
en: O God of infinite mercy! I give thee due thanks, and praise thee
for having admitted me to the confession of my sins
and for having, through thy minister, granted me absolution for them.
I implore thee by the merits of Jesus Christ, thy Son,
of Mary, his most blessed Mother, of the Holy Helpers, and of all the saints,
to accept my confession,
and in thy infinite mercy to condone and amend
all the defects and faults I committed in making it,
and to ratify in heaven the absolution I received on earth.
O my Jesus! How blind I was in not knowing thee
and preferring transitory beauty and earthly attractions to thy grace and love,
and thereby offending thee!
Now I acknowledge my fault,
and am convinced that it is my duty and privilege to love thee above all things.
Too late I have learned it,
but I shall zealously strive to make reparation for my past neglect.
Therefore I renounce the pleasures, vanities, and joys of this deceitful world,
and abhor sin and all that leads to it.
In the future nothing shall ever part me from thy love.
From this moment on I am resolved nevermore to offend thee.
Confirm, O Jesus, this my resolution,
and with thy almighty power strengthen my frailty.
Seal my purpose of amendment with the bestowal of thy grace,
and preserve me in thy grace and love unto the end. Amen.

prayers.title: To Saint Joseph, for Purity
prayers.note: From General Catholic Devotions (New York, 1909), where it is given with an indulgence of Pope Pius IX (1877).
en: Guardian of virgins and father, holy Joseph,
to whose faithful care Christ Jesus, very innocence,
and Mary, Virgin of virgins, were committed;
I pray and beg of thee by these dear pledges, Jesus and Mary,
free me from all uncleanness,
and make me with spotless mind, pure heart, and chaste body,
ever most chastely to serve Jesus and Mary all the days of my life. Amen.

prayers.title: To the Holy Family
prayers.note: From Our Monthly Devotions (New York, 1899), for a household.
en: O most loving Jesus,
who didst hallow by thy surpassing virtues, and the example of thy home life,
the household thou didst choose to live in whilst on earth,
mercifully look down upon this family,
whose members, humbly prostrate before thee, implore thy protection.
Remember that we are thine,
bound and consecrated to thee by a special devotion.
Protect us in thy mercy, deliver us from danger,
help us in our necessities,
and impart to us strength to persevere always in the imitation of thy Holy Family,
so that, by serving thee and loving thee faithfully during this mortal life,
we may at length give thee eternal praise in heaven.
O Mary, dearest Mother, we implore thy assistance,
knowing that thy divine Son will hearken to thy petitions;
and do thou, most glorious patriarch Saint Joseph,
help us with thy powerful patronage,
and place our petitions in Mary’s hands
that she may offer them to Jesus Christ. Amen.

prayers.title: To Saint Michael, Saint Gabriel and Saint Raphael
prayers.note: From Our Monthly Devotions (New York, 1899). The three archangels share a feast on 29 September.
en: Glorious Saint Michael! prince of the heavenly host,
protector of the universal Church,
defend us against all our enemies, visible and invisible.
Do not permit that we should ever fall under their tyranny.
Saint Gabriel! thou who art justly called the strength of God,
since thou hast been chosen to announce to many the mystery of the incarnation,
in which the Almighty has displayed the power of his arms,
make us know the treasure contained in the person of the Son of God,
and be our protector with his august Mother.
Saint Raphael! charitable guide of travellers,
thou who, by divine virtue, dost effect miraculous cures,
deign to guide us in the pilgrimage of this life,
and heal the maladies of our souls and bodies.
All ye orders of blessed spirits,
be our defenders and protectors during our life and at the hour of our death. Amen.

prayers.title: When Someone Has Died
prayers.note: For those who mourn. From Our Monthly Devotions (New York, 1899).
en: Grant, O Lord, we beseech thee,
that while we lament the departure of thy servant,
we may always remember that we are most certainly to follow him (or her).
Give us grace to prepare for that last hour by a good and holy life,
that we may not be taken unprepared by sudden death,
but may be ever on the watch,
that, when thou shalt call, we may go forth to meet the Bridegroom,
and enter with him into glory everlasting.
Through the same Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

prayers.title: The Words of the Saint Benedict Medal
prayers.note: The inscriptions of the medal of Saint Benedict, explained by a manuscript of 1415, said as a prayer in temptation and for a good death. A private prayer of renunciation, not the Church’s rite of exorcism. The Latin is from the Catholic Encyclopedia (1912); the English is the app’s own.
en: ! On the face of the medal, around Saint Benedict
The Cross of our holy father Benedict.
May we be strengthened by his presence at our death.
! On the back, on the arms of the cross
May the holy Cross be my light;
let not the dragon be my guide.
! Around the edge
Begone, Satan; never urge vain things upon me.
What thou offerest is evil; drink thine own poison.
la: Eius in obitu nostro praesentia muniamur.
Vade retro, Satana; nunquam suade mihi vana.
Sunt mala quae libas; ipse venena bibas.

prayers.title: Prayer for a House
prayers.note: The prayer that closes the sprinkling with holy water before Sunday Mass in the Roman Missal of 1962, asking God to send his angel to guard all who dwell in the place. The English is the app’s own.
en: Hear us, O holy Lord, almighty Father, everlasting God,
and vouchsafe to send thy holy Angel from heaven,
to guard, cherish, protect, visit and defend
all who dwell in this house.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Exaudi nos, Domine sancte, Pater omnipotens, aeterne Deus,
et mittere digneris sanctum Angelum tuum de caelis,
qui custodiat, foveat, protegat, visitet atque defendat

prayers.title: A Parent’s Blessing
prayers.note: For a father or mother to bless a child, as the Church’s Book of Blessings allows parents to do. The words are the blessing of the priests of Israel (Numbers 6:24-26), with the sign of the cross.
en: ! Trace a small cross on the child’s forehead with your thumb.
May God bless you, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

prayers.title: O Mary, Conceived without Sin
prayers.note: The words around the Miraculous Medal, shown to Saint Catherine Labouré in 1830.
en: O Mary, conceived without sin,
pray for us who have recourse to thee.
la: ora pro nobis qui ad te confugimus.

prayers.title: Prayer of Saints Simon and Jude
prayers.latin: Deus, qui nos per beatos Apostolos
prayers.note: The prayer of the feast of 28 October in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, who through thy blessed Apostles Simon and Jude
hast brought us to the knowledge of thy name,
grant us to celebrate their everlasting glory by growing in holiness,
and to grow in holiness by celebrating it.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Deus, qui nos per beatos Apostolos tuos Simonem et Iudam
ad agnitionem tui nominis venire tribuisti:
da nobis eorum gloriam sempiternam et proficiendo celebrare,

prayers.title: Prayer of Saints Marcellinus, Peter and Erasmus
prayers.note: The prayer of 2 June in the Roman Missal (1962), which still named Saint Erasmus (Saint Elmo). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, who dost gladden us each year
by the feast of thy blessed Martyrs Marcellinus, Peter and Erasmus,
grant, we beseech thee,
that as we rejoice in their merits,
we may be kindled by their example.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Deus, qui nos annua beatorum Martyrum tuorum
Marcellini, Petri atque Erasmi sollemnitate laetificas:

prayers.title: If You Seek Miracles
prayers.note: The responsory of Saint Anthony of Padua, from the Office written by Julian of Speyer about 1240, with the prayer of his feast. The English is translated for this app.
en: If you seek miracles:
death, error, calamity,
the devil and leprosy flee,
the sick rise up healed.
R. The sea gives way, and chains;
limbs and lost things
are asked for and received
by young and old.
Dangers pass away,
need is ended;
let those who have known it tell it,
let the people of Padua say it.
R. The sea gives way, and chains;
limbs and lost things
are asked for and received
by young and old.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
R. The sea gives way, and chains;
limbs and lost things
are asked for and received
by young and old.
V. Pray for us, blessed Anthony.
R. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
! Let us pray.
May the votive feast of blessed Anthony,
thy Confessor and Doctor,
gladden thy Church, O God,
that she may ever be strengthened with spiritual help
and be found worthy to enjoy everlasting joys.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto.
V. Ora pro nobis, beate Antoni.
R. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.

prayers.title: Prayer of Saint Francis Xavier
prayers.note: The prayer of his feast, 3 December, in the Roman Missal (1962). It closes the Novena of Grace. The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, who willed to gather the peoples of the Indies into thy Church
by the preaching and miracles of blessed Francis,
mercifully grant
that we who honour his glorious merits
may also follow the example of his virtues.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Deus, qui Indiarum gentes beati Francisci
praedicatione et miraculis Ecclesiae tuae aggregare voluisti:

prayers.title: Prayer of Saint Joseph
prayers.note: The prayer of his feast, 19 March, in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
May we be helped, O Lord, we beseech thee,
by the merits of the Spouse of thy most holy Mother,
that what we cannot obtain by our own power
may be given us through his intercession.
Who livest and reignest for ever and ever. Amen.
la: ut, quod possibilitas nostra non obtinet,
Qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum. Amen.

prayers.title: Prayer of the Immaculate Conception
prayers.latin: Deus, qui per immaculatam Virginis Conceptionem
prayers.note: The prayer of the feast of 8 December in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, who by the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin
didst prepare a worthy dwelling for thy Son,
we beseech thee that,
as thou didst preserve her from every stain
by the foreseen death of that same Son,
so thou wouldst grant us also, through her intercession,
to come to thee made clean.
Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Deus, qui per immaculatam Virginis Conceptionem
qui ex morte eiusdem Filii tui praevisa
Per eundem Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.

prayers.title: Prayer of Our Lady of Lourdes
prayers.latin: Deus, qui per immaculatam Virginis Conceptionem
prayers.note: The prayer of 11 February, the Apparition of the Immaculate Virgin, in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, who by the Immaculate Conception of the Virgin
didst prepare a worthy dwelling for thy Son,
we humbly beseech thee
that we who celebrate the Apparition of the same Virgin
may obtain health of mind and body.
Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Deus, qui per immaculatam Virginis Conceptionem
Per eundem Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.

prayers.title: Prayer of Our Lady of Mount Carmel
prayers.note: The prayer of 16 July in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, who hast honoured the Order of Carmel
with the special title of the most blessed ever-Virgin Mary, thy Mother,
mercifully grant
that we who keep her commemoration with solemn office this day
may be defended by her protection
and be found worthy to come to everlasting joys.
Who livest and reignest for ever and ever. Amen.
la: Deus, qui beatissimae semper Virginis et Genetricis tuae Mariae
ut, cuius hodie Commemorationem sollemni celebramus officio,
Qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum. Amen.

prayers.title: Prayer of Our Lady of Sorrows
prayers.note: The prayer of the Seven Sorrows, 15 September, in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, in whose Passion,
according to the prophecy of Simeon,
a sword of sorrow pierced the most sweet soul
of the glorious Virgin and Mother Mary,
mercifully grant
that we who reverently recall her piercing and her suffering,
helped by the glorious merits and prayers
of all the Saints who stood faithfully by the Cross,
may obtain the blessed fruit of thy Passion.
Who livest and reignest for ever and ever. Amen.
la: gloriosae Virginis et Matris Mariae doloris gladius pertransivit:
ut, qui transfixionem eius et passionem venerando recolimus,
omnium Sanctorum Cruci fideliter astantium intercedentibus,
Qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum. Amen.

prayers.title: The Sorrowful Mother Stood
prayers.note: The sequence of Our Lady of Sorrows, thirteenth century, often credited to Jacopone da Todi. The English is translated for this app.
en: The sorrowful Mother stood,
weeping beside the Cross,
while her Son was hanging there.
Through her soul,
groaning, saddened and grieving,
the sword had passed.
O how sad and how afflicted
was that blessed one,
the Mother of the Only-begotten.
She mourned and she grieved,
the loving Mother, as she saw
the torments of her glorious Son.
Who is the man who would not weep
if he saw the Mother of Christ
in such great anguish?
Who could not share her sorrow,
gazing on the Mother of Christ
grieving with her Son?
For the sins of his own people
she saw Jesus in torment
and given up to the scourges.
She saw her own sweet Son
dying, forsaken,
as he gave up his spirit.
Ah, Mother, fountain of love,
make me feel the force of thy sorrow,
that I may mourn with thee.
Make my heart burn
with love of Christ my God,
that I may please him.
Holy Mother, do this for me:
fix the wounds of the Crucified
deep in my heart.
Of thy wounded Son,
who deigned to suffer so much for me,
share the pains with me.
Let me weep lovingly with thee
and suffer with the Crucified
as long as I live.
To stand beside the Cross with thee,
and to be thy companion
in thy weeping, is my desire.
Virgin, most glorious of virgins,
be not bitter to me now;
let me weep with thee.
Let me carry the death of Christ;
make me a sharer in his Passion,
and keep his wounds in mind.
Let me be wounded with his wounds;
let me be filled with the Cross
and with the blood of thy Son.
Lest I burn in the flames,
may I be defended through thee, O Virgin,
on the day of judgement.
Christ, when I must go from here,
grant that through thy Mother I may come
to the palm of victory.
When my body dies,
grant that my soul be given
the glory of paradise. Amen.
la: Quis est homo, qui non fleret,

prayers.title: Prayer of Saint Anne
prayers.note: The prayer of her feast, 26 July, in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, who wast pleased to give blessed Anne the grace
of becoming the mother of her who bore thine only-begotten Son,
mercifully grant
that we who keep her feast
may be helped by her prayers with thee.
Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Deus, qui beatae Annae gratiam conferre dignatus es,
ut Genetricis unigeniti Filii tui mater effici mereretur:
Per eundem Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.

prayers.title: Prayer of Saint Michael and the Angels
prayers.note: The prayer of Saint Michael, 29 September, in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, who in a wonderful order
dost appoint the ministries of Angels and of men,
mercifully grant
that our life on earth may be defended
by those who stand ever before thee
and serve thee in heaven.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: ut, a quibus tibi ministrantibus in caelo semper assistitur,
ab his in terra vita nostra muniatur.

prayers.title: Prayer of Saint Raphael
prayers.note: The prayer of his former feast, 24 October, in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, who gavest the blessed Archangel Raphael
to thy servant Tobias as a companion on his way,
grant to us thy servants
that we may ever be guarded by his care
and strengthened by his help.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Tobiae famulo tuo comitem dedisti in via:

prayers.title: Prayer of Saint Francis of Assisi
prayers.note: The prayer of his feast, 4 October, in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, who through the merits of blessed Francis
dost enlarge thy Church with new children,
grant that, by following him,
we may set little store by earthly things
and ever rejoice in sharing thy heavenly gifts.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Deus, qui Ecclesiam tuam, beati Francisci meritis,
et caelestium donorum semper participatione gaudere.

prayers.title: Prayer of Saint Thérèse
prayers.note: The prayer of her feast in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O Lord, who hast said,
Unless you become as little children,
you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven,
grant us, we beseech thee,
so to follow the footsteps of the holy virgin Thérèse
in humility and simplicity of heart,
that we may obtain the everlasting reward.
Who livest and reignest for ever and ever. Amen.
la: in humilitate et simplicitate cordis vestigia sectari,
Qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum. Amen.

prayers.title: Prayer of Christ the King
prayers.latin: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui in dilecto Filio tuo
prayers.note: The prayer of the feast instituted by Pius XI in 1925, from the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
Almighty, everlasting God,
who in thy beloved Son, the King of all things,
hast willed to restore all things,
mercifully grant
that all the families of the nations,
torn apart by the wound of sin,
may be brought under his most gentle rule.
Who liveth and reigneth with thee for ever and ever. Amen.
la: qui in dilecto Filio tuo, universorum Rege,
Qui tecum vivit et regnat in saecula saeculorum. Amen.

prayers.title: Prayer of the Sacred Heart
prayers.latin: Deus, qui nobis in Corde Filii tui
prayers.note: The prayer of the feast of the Sacred Heart in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, who in the Heart of thy Son,
wounded by our sins,
dost mercifully bestow on us
the infinite treasures of thy love,
grant, we beseech thee,
that as we offer him the devout homage of our love,
we may also make him worthy amends.
Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Deus, qui nobis in Corde Filii tui,
ut, illi devotum pietatis nostrae praestantes obsequium,
Per eundem Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.

prayers.title: Prayer of Saint Benedict
prayers.note: The prayer for an abbot in the Roman Missal (1962), said on his feast. The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
May the intercession of blessed Benedict the Abbot
commend us to thee, O Lord, we beseech thee,
that what we cannot obtain by our own merits
we may obtain through his prayers.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: ut, quod nostris meritis non valemus,

prayers.title: Prayer of Saint Patrick
prayers.note: The prayer of his feast, 17 March, in the Roman Missal (1962). The English is translated for this app.
en: ! Let us pray.
O God, who didst send blessed Patrick,
thy Confessor and Bishop,
to preach thy glory to the nations,
grant, through his merits and intercession,
that by thy mercy we may be able to fulfil
what thou commandest us to do.
Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
la: Deus, qui ad praedicandam gentibus gloriam tuam

prayers.title: Opening of Night Prayer
prayers.note: The opening of Compline, the Church’s prayer at night. The English of the blessing is from E. J. Quigley, The Divine Office (1920); the versicle is Psalm 70.
en: The Lord almighty grant us a quiet night and a perfect end. Amen.
V. O God, come to my assistance.
R. O Lord, make haste to help me.
> glory-be
la: Noctem quietam et finem perfectum concedat nobis Dominus omnipotens. Amen.
V. Deus, in adiutorium meum intende.
R. Domine, ad adiuvandum me festina.

prayers.title: Into Thy Hands
prayers.note: The responsory of Compline, from Psalms 31 and 17. The English is from E. J. Quigley, The Divine Office (1920).
en: V. Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit.
R. Into thy hands I commend my spirit.
V. For thou hast redeemed us, O Lord God of truth.
R. I commend my spirit.
V. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
R. Into thy hands, O Lord, I commend my spirit.
V. Keep us, O Lord, as the apple of thine eye.
R. Protect us under the shadow of thy wings.
la: V. In manus tuas, Domine, commendo spiritum meum.
R. In manus tuas, Domine, commendo spiritum meum.
V. Redemisti nos, Domine, Deus veritatis.
V. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto.
R. In manus tuas, Domine, commendo spiritum meum.
V. Custodi nos, Domine, ut pupillam oculi.
R. Sub umbra alarum tuarum protege nos.

prayers.title: The Song of Simeon at Night
prayers.note: The Song of Simeon as said at Compline, with its antiphon. The English of the antiphon is from E. J. Quigley, The Divine Office (1920).
en: Save us, O Lord, while we are awake, and guard us when we sleep, that we may watch with Christ and rest in peace.
> glory-be
Save us, O Lord, while we are awake, and guard us when we sleep, that we may watch with Christ and rest in peace.
la: Salva nos, Domine, vigilantes, custodi nos dormientes, ut vigilemus cum Christo et requiescamus in pace.
quia viderunt oculi mei salutare tuum,
quod parasti ante faciem omnium populorum,
Salva nos, Domine, vigilantes, custodi nos dormientes, ut vigilemus cum Christo et requiescamus in pace.

prayers.title: Close of Night Prayer
prayers.note: The closing prayer and blessing of Compline. The English of the blessing is from E. J. Quigley, The Divine Office (1920).
en: ! Let us pray.
> night-prayer
May the almighty and merciful Lord, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, bless and preserve us. Amen.
la: Benedicat et custodiat nos omnipotens et misericors Dominus, Pater, et Filius, et Spiritus Sanctus. Amen.

prayers.title: Prayer before Mass
prayers.note: From General Catholic Devotions (New York, 1909).
en: Almighty and eternal God, I appear in thy presence
to assist at the most holy sacrifice of the body and blood
of Jesus Christ, thy Son, my Redeemer,
and to offer it up jointly with the priest and the faithful here present,
in grateful remembrance of his passion and death,
for the promotion of thy glory, and for my salvation.
Together with all the holy Masses that are celebrated throughout the world,
I offer up this august sacrifice for the following intentions:
to adore thee, O my God, as thou dost deserve to be adored;
to give thee due thanks for the innumerable benefits which I owe to thy bounty;
to make reparation for the many offences I have committed;
to appease thy just anger,
and to invoke thy infinite mercy for me, for thy holy Church,
for the whole world, and for the souls in purgatory. Amen.

prayers.title: Offering a Suffering
prayers.note: In the app’s own words.
en: Lord Jesus Christ, I give thee what I am suffering now.
I would not have chosen it,
and thou knowest how heavy it is.
I join it to thy Passion and thy Cross:
take it, and let it serve thee,
for the one I name before thee, and for thy Church.
Give me patience for this hour,
humility to accept the help I am given,
and trust that nothing given to thee is lost.
Into thy hands I commend my spirit. Amen.

prayers.title: Three Hail Marys
prayers.note: An old custom, morning and night, asking Our Lady’s help to keep pure in mind and body. Saint Alphonsus Liguori commended it.
en: ! In honour of the purity of the Blessed Virgin, and asking her help to keep pure:
> hail-mary x3

prayers.title: The Seven Sorrows and Joys of Saint Joseph
prayers.note: Said on each of the seven Sundays before the feast of Saint Joseph, or at any time. From Our Monthly Devotions (New York, 1899).
en: # First sorrow and joy

O glorious Saint Joseph, most pure spouse of thy most holy Mary, even as the trouble and anguish of thy heart was great in the perplexity of abandoning thy most chaste and stainless spouse, so, too, inexplicable was thy delight when by the angel was revealed to thee the sovereign mystery of the incarnation.
Through this sorrow and this joy of thine, we pray thee, now and in our last agony, to comfort our soul with the joy of a good life, and of a holy death, like unto thine between Jesus and Mary.
> our-father
> hail-mary
> glory-be
# Second sorrow and joy

O glorious Saint Joseph, most blessed patriarch, who wast selected for the office of reputed father of the Word made man, the grief which thou didst feel at seeing the Child Jesus born in such great poverty was suddenly changed for thee into heavenly exultation at hearing the angelic harmony, and seeing the glories of that most resplendent night.

Through this sorrow and this joy of thine, we beseech thee to obtain for us that, after the journey of this life is over, we may pass hence to hear the angelic praises, and to enjoy the splendors of the glory of heaven.
> our-father
> hail-mary
> glory-be
# Third sorrow and joy

O glorious Saint Joseph, who didst fulfil most obediently all God’s commands, the most precious blood which the Child Redeemer shed in the circumcision struck death into thy heart, but the name of Jesus revived it, and filled it full of joy.

Through this sorrow and this joy of thine, obtain for us that, all vices having been taken from us during life, we may expire in exultation with the most holy name of Jesus in our hearts and upon our lips.
> our-father
> hail-mary
> glory-be
# Fourth sorrow and joy

O most glorious Saint Joseph, most faithful saint, who wast a partaker in the mysteries of our redemption, if Simeon’s prophecy of that which Jesus and Mary were to suffer caused thee a mortal pang, it filled thee also with a blessed joy at the salvation and glorious resurrection of innumerable souls, which he at the same time foretold would thence proceed.

Through this sorrow and this joy of thine, obtain for us that we may be of the number of those who, through the merits of Jesus, and at the intercession of the Virgin Mother, are to rise again in glory.
> our-father
> hail-mary
> glory-be
# Fifth sorrow and joy

O glorious Saint Joseph, most watchful guardian and familiar attendant of the incarnate Son of God, how much didst thou suffer in supporting and in serving the Son of the Most High, particularly in the flight which thou hadst to make into Egypt; but how much again didst thou rejoice at having always with thee that same God, and at seeing the idols of Egypt fall to the ground.

Through this sorrow and this joy of thine, obtain for us that, by keeping far from us hell’s tyrant, especially by flying from dangerous occasions, every idol of earthly affection may fall from our hearts; and that, wholly occupied in the service of Jesus and of Mary, we may live for them alone, and die a happy death.
> our-father
> hail-mary
> glory-be
# Sixth sorrow and joy

O glorious Saint Joseph, angel of the earth, who didst marvel at beholding the King of heaven subject to thy commands, if thy consolation at bringing him back from Egypt was disturbed by the fear of Archelaus, yet, assured by the angel, thou didst with Jesus and Mary dwell in joy at Nazareth.

Through this sorrow and this joy of thine, obtain for us that our heart, unclouded by hurtful fears, may enjoy peace of conscience, and that we may live secure with Jesus and Mary, and with them may also die.
> our-father
> hail-mary
> glory-be
# Seventh sorrow and joy

O glorious Saint Joseph, model of all holiness, when, without fault of thine, thou hadst lost the Child Jesus, thou didst seek him for three days in the greatest sorrow, until with joyful heart thou didst possess again thy life, finding him in the Temple, among the doctors.

Through this sorrow and this joy of thine, with fervent sighs we supplicate thee to interpose in our behalf, that so it may never befall us to lose Jesus by mortal sin; but that, if unhappily we ever lose him, we may seek him again with unwearied sorrow, until once more we find his favor, especially at the moment of our death, that so we may pass to the enjoyment of him in heaven, and there, with thee, sing his divine mercies for all eternity.
> our-father
> hail-mary
> glory-be
Ant. Jesus himself was beginning about his thirtieth year, being (as it was supposed) the son of Joseph.
V. Pray for us, O holy Joseph.
R. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
! Let us pray.

O God, who by thy ineffable providence didst vouchsafe to choose the blessed Joseph for the spouse of thy most holy Mother; grant, we beseech thee, that he whom we venerate as our protector on earth may be our intercessor in heaven; who livest and reignest forever and ever. Amen.

prayers.title: Choosing Saint Joseph as Patron
prayers.note: A short act of entrustment to Saint Joseph, from Our Monthly Devotions (New York, 1899).
en: O blessed Joseph, faithful guardian of my Redeemer, Jesus Christ, protector of thy chaste spouse, the Virgin Mother of God, I choose thee this day to be my special patron and advocate, and I firmly resolve to honor thee from this time forth.

Therefore I humbly beseech thee to receive me as thy client, to instruct me in every doubt, to comfort me in every affliction, to obtain for me and for all the knowledge and love of the Heart of Jesus, and finally to defend and protect me at the hour of death. Amen.

prayers.title: Consecration to the Heart of Mary
prayers.note: From Our Monthly Devotions (New York, 1899), where it opens September, the month of the Heart of Mary.
en: O heart of Mary, I offer, I consecrate to thee my heart!
Thou shalt be the object of my veneration, love and confidence;
I will pay thee my devotions every day;
I will celebrate thy feasts with joy;
I will proclaim thy greatness and thy goodness without ceasing.
I will neglect no means of obtaining for thee the honor and the homage which are due unto thee.
I will bring all the thoughts and affections of my heart into conformity with thine, and I will make it my duty to imitate thy virtues, especially thy purity and thy humility.
Vouchsafe, O Mary, to open thy heart and receive me therein. Amen.

prayers.title: An Offering to the Sacred Heart
prayers.note: The first part of an act of oblation in General Catholic Devotions (New York, 1909).
en: Divine Heart of my Jesus!
I adore thee with all the powers of my soul, which I consecrate to thee for ever, with my thoughts, my words, my works, and my whole self.
I purpose to offer to thee, as far as I can, acts of adoration, love, and glory, like unto those which thou offerest to thy eternal Father.
Be thou, I beseech thee, the repairer of my transgressions, the protector of my life, my refuge and asylum in the hour of death.

By thy sighs, and by that sea of bitterness in which thou wast plunged for me throughout thy whole mortal life, grant me true contrition for my sins, contempt of earthly things, a burning desire of eternal glory, trust in thy infinite merits, and final perseverance in thy grace.

prayers.title: Thirty Days’ Prayer to Saint Joseph
prayers.note: Traditionally said for thirty days for one intention. From Our Monthly Devotions (New York, 1899). It repeats two pious opinions the Church does not teach: that Saint Joseph himself performed the circumcision, and that he was taken body and soul into heaven when Christ ascended.
en: Ever-blessed and glorious Joseph, kind and indulgent father, and compassionate friend of all in sorrow, through that bitter grief with which thy heart was saturated, when thou didst behold the sufferings of the Infant Saviour, and in thy prophetic view didst contemplate his most ignominious Passion and death, take pity, I beseech thee, on my poverty and necessities, counsel me in my doubts, and console me in all my anxieties.
Thou art the good father and protector of orphans, the advocate of the defenceless, the patron of those who are in need and desolation.
Do not, then, disregard the petition of thy poor child; my sins have drawn down upon me the just displeasure of my God, and hence I am surrounded with sorrows.
To thee, O amiable guardian of the poor neglected family of Nazareth, do I fly for shelter and protection.
Listen, then, I entreat of thee, with a father’s solicitude, to the earnest prayer of thy poor supplicant, and obtain for me the objects of my petition.
I ask it by the infinite mercy of the eternal Son of God, which induced him to assume our nature and be born into this world of sorrow.
I ask it by the grief which filled thy heart when, ignorant of the mystery wrought in thy immaculate spouse, thou didst fear thou shouldst be separated from her.

I ask it by that weariness, solicitude, and suffering which thou didst endure when thou soughtest in vain at the inns of Bethlehem a shelter for the sacred Virgin and a birthplace for the Infant God, and when, being everywhere refused, thou wert obliged to consent that the Queen of heaven should give birth to the world’s Redeemer in a wretched stable.

I ask it by that most sad and painful duty imposed on thee when, the divine Child being eight days old, thou wert obliged to inflict a deep wound on his tender body, and thus be the first to make flow that sacred blood which was to wash away the sins of the world.
I ask it by the sweetness and power of that sacred name, Jesus, which thou didst confer on the adorable Infant.
I ask it by that mortal anguish inflicted on thee by the prophecy of holy Simeon, which declared the Child Jesus and his holy Mother the future victims of their love and our sins.

I ask it through that sorrow and anguish which filled thy soul when the angel declared to thee that the life of the Child Jesus was sought by his enemies, from whose impious designs thou wert obliged to fly with him and his blessed Mother into Egypt.
I ask it by all the pains, fatigues, and toils of that long and perilous pilgrimage.
I ask it by all the sorrows thou didst endure when in Egypt thou wert not able, even by the sweat of thy brow, to procure poor food and clothing for thy most poor family.
I ask it by all the grief thou didst feel each time the divine Child asked for a morsel of bread, and thou hadst it not to give him.
I ask it by all thy solicitude to preserve the sacred Child and the immaculate Mary during thy second journey, when thou wert ordered to return to thy native country.
I ask it by thy peaceful dwelling in Nazareth, in which so many joys and sorrows were mingled.
I ask it by thy extreme affliction in being deprived three days of the company of the adorable Child.
I ask it by thy joy at finding him in the Temple, and by the ineffable consolation imparted to thee in the cottage of Nazareth with the company and society of the little Jesus.
I ask it by that wonderful condescension by which he subjected himself to thy will.
I ask it through that dolorous view, continually in thy mind, of all thy Jesus was to suffer.

I ask it by that painful contemplation, which made thee foresee the divine little hands and feet, now so active in serving thee, one day to be pierced with cruel nails; that head which rested gently on thy bosom, crowned with sharp thorns; that delicate body which thou didst tenderly fold in thy mantle and press to thy heart, stripped and extended on a cross.
I ask it by that heroic sacrifice of thy will and best affection by which thou didst offer up to the eternal Father the last awful moment when the Man-God was to expire for our salvation.
I ask it by that perfect love and conformity with which thou didst receive the divine order to depart from this life, and from the company of Jesus and Mary.

I ask it by that exceeding great joy which filled thy soul when the Redeemer of the world, triumphant over death and hell, entered into the possession of his kingdom, and conducted thee also into it with especial honors.
I ask it through Mary’s glorious assumption, and through that interminable bliss, which with her, thou wilt eternally derive from the presence of God.
O good father!
I beseech thee by all thy sufferings, sorrows, and joys, to hear me and to obtain the grant of my earnest petitions.
! Here name them or reflect on them.

Obtain for all those who have asked thy prayers all that is useful to them in the designs of God; and finally, my dear protector, be thou with me and all who are dear to me in our last moments, that we may eternally chant the praises of Jesus, Mary, and Joseph. Amen.

prayers.title: Renewal of Baptismal Promises
prayers.note: The questions of baptism, renewed at the Easter Vigil and fitting on the anniversary of your own. The English is translated for this app from the traditional Latin.
en: ! Said alone, answer each question yourself, aloud or in the heart.
V. Do you renounce Satan?
R. I do renounce him.
V. And all his works?
R. I do renounce them.
V. And all his pomps?
R. I do renounce them.
V. Do you believe in God, the Father almighty, Creator of heaven and earth?
R. I do believe.
V. Do you believe in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, who was born and who suffered?
R. I do believe.
V. Do you believe also in the Holy Spirit, the holy Catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and life everlasting?
R. I do believe.
> our-father

prayers.title: Hail, Star of the Sea
prayers.note: A hymn of the ninth century, sung at Vespers on the feasts of Our Lady. Saint Louis de Montfort asks for it each day of the preparation for consecration. The English is translated for this app.
en: Hail, star of the sea,
loving Mother of God,
and Virgin for ever,
happy gate of heaven.
Taking that Ave
from Gabriel’s mouth,
establish us in peace,
and turn the name of Eva round.
Loose the bonds of the guilty,
bring light to the blind,
drive away our evils,
ask for every good.
Show thyself a mother:
through thee may he receive our prayers
who, born for us,
chose to be thine own.
Virgin without equal,
meek above all others,
make us, freed from our faults,
meek and chaste.
Grant us a pure life,
make our way safe,
that seeing Jesus
we may rejoice with thee for ever.
Praise be to God the Father,
glory to Christ most high,
and to the Holy Spirit:
to the three one honour. Amen.

prayers.title: O Jesus, Living in Mary
prayers.note: A prayer of the French school of the seventeenth century, from Father Charles de Condren and Father Jean-Jacques Olier, which Saint Louis de Montfort asks for in the last week of the preparation for consecration. The English is translated for this app.
en: O Jesus, living in Mary,
come and live in thy servants,
in the spirit of thy holiness,
in the fullness of thy power,
in the perfection of thy ways,
in the truth of thy virtues,
in the communion of thy mysteries;
overcome every power that is against thee,
in thy Spirit, for the glory of the Father. Amen.
la: veni et vive in famulis tuis,
in Spiritu tuo, ad gloriam Patris. Amen.

prayers.title: Saint Joseph, Be Mindful of Me
prayers.note: From Our Monthly Devotions (New York, 1899), where it closes each day of the month of Saint Joseph.
en: Holy Saint Joseph, spouse of Mary,
be mindful of me, pray for me, watch over me.
Guardian of the paradise of the new Adam,
provide for my temporal wants.
Faithful guardian of the most precious of all treasures,
I beseech thee to bring this matter to a happy end,
if it be for the glory of God and the good of my soul. Amen.

prayers.title: Most Glorious Prince, Saint Michael
prayers.note: The antiphon at the Magnificat of Second Vespers of the feast of Saint Michael, 29 September, in the Roman Breviary. The English is translated for this app.
en: Most glorious prince, Michael the Archangel,
be mindful of us:
here and everywhere,
pray always for us to the Son of God.
la: semper precare pro nobis Filium Dei.

prayers.title: Most Glorious Prince, Saint Raphael
prayers.note: The antiphon at the Magnificat of Second Vespers of Saint Raphael (24 October) in the Roman Breviary, as it stood until 1969. The English is translated for this app.
en: Most glorious prince, Raphael the Archangel,
be mindful of us:
here and everywhere,
pray always for us to the Son of God.
la: semper precare pro nobis Filium Dei.

prayers.title: Holy Apostle Paul
prayers.note: An antiphon of the Roman Breviary for the Commemoration of Saint Paul (30 June). The English is translated for this app.
en: Holy Paul the Apostle,
preacher of the truth and teacher of the nations,
intercede for us with God, who chose thee.
la: intercede pro nobis ad Deum, qui te elegit.

prayers.title: Priest of God, Martin
prayers.note: An antiphon of the Roman Breviary for Saint Martin of Tours (11 November). The English is translated for this app.
en: Priest of God, Martin, excellent shepherd,
pray to God for us.

prayers.title: O Excellent Teacher
prayers.note: The antiphon at the Magnificat of both Vespers in the Common of Doctors of the Church in the Roman Breviary, said on the feast of any Doctor. At “N.” say the saint’s name. The English is translated for this app.
en: O excellent teacher, light of holy Church,
blessed N., lover of the law of God,
pray for us to the Son of God.
la: O Doctor optime, Ecclesiae sanctae lumen,

prayers.title: Priest and Bishop
prayers.note: The antiphon at the Magnificat of First Vespers in the Common of a Confessor Bishop in the Roman Breviary, said on the eve of the feasts of holy bishops who were not martyrs. The English is translated for this app.
en: Priest and bishop, and worker of virtues,
good shepherd among the people,
pray to the Lord for us.
la: Sacerdos et Pontifex, et virtutum opifex,

novenas.name: Novena to Saint Jude
novenas.about: Nine days with the apostle Jude Thaddeus, whom many invoke in hard and hopeless cases. Its heart is his own letter: keep yourselves in the love of God.
novenas.when: Traditionally 19 to 27 October, ending on the eve of Saints Simon and Jude. The Chicago shrine’s first solemn novena (1929) closed on the feast itself, so 20 to 28 October is also kept. It may be made at any time.
novenas.note: The chain prayer printed in newspapers, said nine times a day and “never known to fail” if published, is not this devotion: no number of repetitions or printed notice obliges God. “Patron of hopeless cases” is a popular title, not a teaching.

novenas.name: Novena to Saint Elmo (Saint Erasmus)
novenas.about: Saint Erasmus, bishop and martyr, called Saint Elmo, one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers: patron of sailors and of those who suffer pain in the stomach and bowels.
novenas.when: Traditionally 24 May to 1 June, ending on the eve of his day, 2 June.
novenas.note: “Elmo” is an old contraction of Erasmus. His Acts are largely legend; the picture of a windlass is a sailors’ emblem, and the Martyrology says he died in peace. He left the General Calendar in 1969 but remains in the Roman Martyrology. In Spain and Portugal “San Telmo” usually means Blessed Peter González, who has a novena of his own here.

novenas.name: Novena to Blessed Peter González (San Telmo)
novenas.about: The Dominican preacher of Galicia, patron of Spanish and Portuguese sailors, whom they call San Telmo or Saint Elmo.
novenas.when: 5 to 13 April, ending on the eve of his day in the Dominican calendar. It often falls in Lent or Holy Week; it may be made at any time.
novenas.note: He is a Blessed, beatified in the thirteenth century and never canonized. The Dominicans keep him on 14 April.

novenas.name: Novena of the Divine Mercy
novenas.about: Nine days of the Chaplet of Divine Mercy, from Good Friday to the eve of Divine Mercy Sunday, each day bringing a different group of souls to the mercy of Christ.
novenas.when: Good Friday to the Saturday after Easter (the eve of the Second Sunday of Easter). It may also be made at any time.

perDay.title: All mankind
perDay.intention: All people, and above all sinners: that they may be drowned in the sea of his mercy.

perDay.title: Priests and religious
perDay.intention: Priests and those consecrated to God, through whom his mercy flows to others.

perDay.title: The faithful
perDay.intention: All devout and faithful souls, who consoled him on the way of the Cross.

perDay.title: Those who do not know him
perDay.intention: Those who do not believe in God, and those who do not yet know Christ.

perDay.title: Christians separated from the Church
perDay.intention: Those who have separated themselves from the unity of the Church.

perDay.title: The meek and humble, and children
perDay.intention: The meek and humble of heart and little children, whom he holds closest.

perDay.title: Those who honour his mercy
perDay.intention: Those who especially honour and spread his mercy, and live by it.

perDay.title: The souls in purgatory
perDay.intention: The holy souls, that they may be freed by the merits of his Passion.

perDay.title: The lukewarm
perDay.intention: Lukewarm souls, who caused him the greatest sorrow in the Garden.

novenas.note: Each day’s intention follows Saint Faustina’s Diary. The promises she recorded there are private revelation: the Church approves the devotion and its feast, and does not guarantee the promises apart from faith and trust.

novenas.name: Novena to the Holy Spirit
novenas.about: The first novena: the nine days the apostles waited in prayer with Mary between the Ascension and Pentecost. One gift of the Spirit for each day.
novenas.when: From the Friday after Ascension Thursday to the Saturday before Pentecost (Easter + 40 to Easter + 48 days), whether or not the Ascension is transferred to Sunday in one’s diocese. It may also be made at any time of year.

perDay.title: The Promise
perDay.intention: That we may wait for the Spirit as the apostles did, with Mary, in one mind and in prayer.

perDay.title: Fear of the Lord
perDay.intention: Reverence and a horror of offending God, out of love rather than dread.

perDay.title: Piety
perDay.intention: The heart of a child towards God as Father, and kindness towards others.

perDay.title: Fortitude
perDay.intention: Strength to do good and to bear trials, and to persevere.

perDay.title: Knowledge
perDay.intention: To see created things truly, and to use them in the right way.

perDay.title: Understanding
perDay.intention: Light to enter into the truths of faith.

perDay.title: Counsel
perDay.intention: To know what to do and choose rightly, especially in hard cases.

perDay.title: Wisdom
perDay.intention: To taste the things of God and to judge all things by him.

perDay.title: The fruits of the Spirit
perDay.intention: That the gifts may bear fruit in charity, joy and peace.

novenas.name: Novena to the Sacred Heart
novenas.about: Nine days ending on the eve of the feast of the Sacred Heart, with its litany.
novenas.when: The feast is the Friday after the Second Sunday after Pentecost (19 days after Pentecost). The novena runs from the Wednesday after Trinity Sunday to the Thursday before the feast. Some end on the feast itself (Thursday after Trinity Sunday to the Friday).
novenas.note: The promises to Saint Margaret Mary are her private revelation; none of them is a guarantee apart from faith and a good life.

novenas.name: Novena to Saint Joseph
novenas.about: Prayed from 10 to 18 March, ending on the eve of his feast.
novenas.when: 10 to 18 March. When the solemnity is transferred (if 19 March falls on a Sunday of Lent or in Holy Week), the reader may end on the eve of the day it is kept or simply keep 10 to 18 March; both are fine.

novenas.name: Novena for the Immaculate Conception
novenas.about: Prayed from 29 November to 7 December, ending on the eve of the feast.
novenas.when: 29 November to 7 December.

novenas.name: Novena to Our Lady of Guadalupe
novenas.about: Nine days before the feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe, patroness of the Americas and protectress of the unborn.
novenas.when: 3 to 11 December, ending on the eve; in Mexico the night of 11 to 12 December is kept with the song Las Mañanitas. Some parishes pray 4 to 12 December.

novenas.name: Novena to Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal
novenas.about: Nine days before 27 November, the day in 1830 when Saint Catherine Labouré saw the design of the medal: ’O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to thee.’
novenas.when: 18 to 26 November. Many parishes also keep a perpetual novena each week, on a day that varies from place to place.
novenas.note: The medal is a sacramental, not a charm: it helps through the Church’s prayer and our faith.

novenas.name: Novena to Our Mother of Perpetual Help
novenas.about: Nine days, or a weekly novena kept for years in Redemptorist churches, before the icon of Our Mother of Perpetual Help.
novenas.when: 18 to 26 June, before the feast of 27 June, which the Redemptorists and some places keep; it is not in the General Calendar. Many Redemptorist churches keep a perpetual novena each week, on a day that varies from place to place.

novenas.name: Novena to Saint Thérèse
novenas.about: Nine days with the saint of the little way: trust and love in small things, as a child with its Father.
novenas.when: 22 to 30 September, ending on the eve of her feast (1 October since 1969; 3 October before).
novenas.note: Some ask for a rose as a sign that the prayer is heard. Signs are not promised, and their absence says nothing.

novenas.name: Novena to Saint Anthony of Padua
novenas.about: Nine days, or nine or thirteen Tuesdays, with Saint Anthony, preacher and Doctor of the Church, whom many ask to help them find what is lost.
novenas.when: 4 to 12 June, ending on the eve of his feast. Alternatively on nine or thirteen consecutive Tuesdays before 13 June, or at any time.
novenas.note: Bargaining with the saint, or turning his statue to the wall until something is found, is superstition. The responsory praises God’s power in his saint; it is not a guarantee.

novenas.name: Novena to Saint Michael the Archangel
novenas.about: Nine days before Michaelmas, asking Saint Michael’s protection in the battle against evil.
novenas.when: 20 to 28 September.

novenas.name: Novena for the Assumption
novenas.about: Nine days before Our Lady’s Assumption into heaven, body and soul.
novenas.when: 6 to 14 August.

novenas.name: Novena to Our Lady of Lourdes
novenas.about: Nine days before 11 February, the day of the first apparition to Saint Bernadette in 1858; also the World Day of the Sick.
novenas.when: 2 to 10 February.
novenas.note: Lourdes water is a sign of prayer and penance, not a remedy in itself. Pray for healing, and for the grace to bear illness.

novenas.name: Novena to Saint Anne
novenas.about: Nine days with the mother of Our Lady, patron of mothers and grandmothers.
novenas.when: 17 to 25 July.
novenas.note: Her name and story come from an early book outside Scripture, the Protoevangelium of James.

novenas.name: Novena to Saint Rita
novenas.about: Nine days with Saint Rita of Cascia, wife, widow and Augustinian nun, invoked in impossible causes and in troubled marriages; a teacher of forgiveness.
novenas.when: 13 to 21 May.
novenas.note: Much of her life was written down long after her death, and some of it is legend. What tradition reports with most confidence is her forgiveness of those who killed her husband.

novenas.name: Novena to Saint Peregrine
novenas.about: Nine days with the Servite friar of Forlì, healed of a cancerous leg in prayer before the crucifix, and patron of those with cancer and other grave illness.
novenas.when: 22 to 30 April, ending on the eve of 1 May, his day in the Roman Martyrology; many Servite communities keep him on 4 May. Often prayed at any time for someone who is ill.
novenas.note: Prayer for healing goes with medical care, never instead of it. His cure is a tradition of his order, the Servants of Mary.

novenas.name: Novena to the Infant Jesus of Prague
novenas.about: Nine days of trust in the Child Jesus, honoured in the small statue kept by the Carmelites of Prague since 1628.
novenas.when: Any time. Some pray it in the nine days before Christmas, or from the 17th to the 25th of a month, the 25th recalling Christmas. At Prague the feast is kept on 14 January.
novenas.note: Sayings that those who honour the statue “will never be poor”, or that an hourly novena is sure to be answered, are legend, not the Church’s teaching.

novenas.name: Novena to Saint Francis of Assisi
novenas.about: Nine days with the poor man of Assisi, who gloried only in the Cross of Christ.
novenas.when: 25 September to 3 October; Franciscans keep the evening of 3 October as the Transitus, the hour of his death.
novenas.note: The prayer “Lord, make me an instrument of your peace” is not by Saint Francis; it was written in the twentieth century.

novenas.name: Novena to Christ the King
novenas.about: Nine days before the last Sunday of the Church’s year, asking that Christ reign in our hearts, homes and nations.
novenas.when: The feast is the last Sunday before Advent (between 20 and 26 November). The novena runs from the Friday nine days before to the Saturday eve (13 to 21 November in 2026). From 1925 to 1969 the feast was the last Sunday of October.

novenas.name: Novena to Our Lady of Mount Carmel
novenas.about: Nine days with Mary as Mother and Beauty of Carmel, before the feast of 16 July.
novenas.when: 7 to 15 July.
novenas.note: The Brown Scapular is a sign of belonging to Mary and of a Christian life, not a charm; see the guide under Tools.

novenas.name: Novena to Our Lady of Sorrows
novenas.about: Nine days with Mary at the Cross: one of her seven sorrows on each of the first seven days, then her motherhood given to us, and her silent faith.
novenas.when: 6 to 14 September, ending on the eve of the feast (the eve is the Exaltation of the Cross).

perDay.intention: To stand with Mary in this sorrow, and to learn from her to suffer with Christ.
